claim: REFUTED. The effect slot of `status` takes a BARE content name (`status false unmoving @unit 60`); it is not a variable read and it must NOT carry the @ prefix. The old claim (bare name reads null, needs `@unmoving`) was exactly backwards.
why: ApplyEffectI stores the effect as a plain java String: LStatements.java:1618 `new ApplyEffectI(clear, effect, builder.var(unit), builder.var(duration))` -- only unit and duration become LVars. LExecutor.java:1743 resolves it with `content.statusEffect(effect)` -> ContentLoader.getByName (ContentLoader.java:228-240) = exact map lookup on the raw token, no '@' stripping, no null-variable indirection. The `!= null` guard in the same line turns an unresolvable name into a silent no-op, which is why the @-prefixed form does nothing and the bare form works. The root cause of the old rule was a bad data row: tools/instr_semantics.json listed status uses=[1,2], i.e. it modelled the effect slot as a variable read. Fixed to uses=[2,3] on 2026-10-25. Scale of the false positive: 3168 INFO hits over ~1400 saves in the 1421-save corpus sweep (out/_bench/sweep-full.md), i.e. ~19% of all findings in that run. The old indirection `LAssembler.var() only resolves @name against GlobalVars` never applied to this field.
state: refuted -- the effect slot is a literal string, not a variable read (the claim had the fix backwards); replaced by the slot check in tools/mlogcheck.py ('in the effect slot is not a content constant' / 'is not a status effect this build knows')
